utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case please, Mr. Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-02-60-T, the Prosecutor versus Vidoje Blagojevic and Dragan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Good morning, everybody. Before we hear the witness, are there any matters that the parties would like to bring to the attention of this Bench? I see none. Madam Usher, could we have the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration in accordance with the paper Madam Usher is showing to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good morning. Examined by Mr. Karnavas:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You may need to speak up a little bit louder. Okay?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if you could please tell us what your name is.

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: My name is Rodoljub Trisic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you please tell us your last name letter by letter.

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: T-r-i-s-i-c.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Trisic, where are you from?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: I am from Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know Mr. Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know him?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: What did you say?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How is it that you know him?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: Well, I know him because we're both from the same place, from Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did you know him growing up?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Trisic, what do you do for a living?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: I work as a transporter. I have three buses, and I work with those buses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Prior to the war, what was your job?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: I was a driver in the Vihor Bratunac transport company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I want to focus your attention around July 1995. Okay. What was your job back then?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: I had a private bus and I worked with that bus. I would do private tours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Could you please tell us what kind of tours you would do.

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: Well, mostly I do shopping tours, Subotica-Novi Sad [as interpreted] was the route, there and back. I didn't have to do my military service, so that's what I did in order to make a living for myself and my family.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, why did you not have to do your military service?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: Because in 1990 I'd had an operation on my right lung, and I was deemed incapable for military service, so I was exempt.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Prior to the fall of Srebrenica, were you mobilised?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, when Srebrenica fell, which is July 11, 1995, were you at that point in time a member of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For how long had you been with the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: All in all, that wartime service, if I can put it that way, was eight months.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. At what point in time did you start your wartime service with the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: Perhaps about a month before the fall of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And with which unit were you serving?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: I served in the 2nd Battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And who was your battalion commander?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: It was Goran Stakic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was your function with the 2nd Battalion?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: Well, I was sort of commander for the security of the command of that 2nd Battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did that entail?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: I had seven invalids, elderly persons, and they were sort of guards in front of the headquarters of that 2nd Battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So basically you were guarding the headquarters of the battalion?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, during the attack on Srebrenica, did you participate in any of those events?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, as I indicated, Srebrenica fell on July 11, 1995. Do you recall what you were doing on that day, the day that Srebrenica fell?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: I received from -- or rather, somebody signed a piece of paper mobilising my bus for transport, requisitioning it. So I complained a little, and then I went home. And my wife called them up to tell them that I was in another battalion. And then they gave me this call-up, these call-up papers, and then I went to the municipality to see what right they had to requisition that bus of mine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let me stop you here. We're going to go step by step. Was that July 11, the day that Srebrenica fell, the actual day when Srebrenica fell? Or could that have been the next day or two days later or three days later? Do you --

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, that was the day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And where did this courier come from?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: From the municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so -- and who from the municipality exactly?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: Well, the civilian authorities, I suppose, and those who were in charge of the mobilisation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was in charge of the mobilisation?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: Well, there was Aco Tesic, and then there was --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. And how were you notified?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: Well, they sent me a piece of paper for the mobilisation of my bus.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, how did they know where to find you?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: They knew I was in the 2nd Battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, when you received this paper, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: I was angry, so I went to the municipality to see them and to ask them who had the right to send me a paper to requisition my bus.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you -- how did you get to the municipality?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: I went with a vehicle belonging -- in a vehicle belonging to the battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: The command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before leaving did you get permission to go to the municipality?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: Well, I didn't ask anybody because the command of the battalion wasn't there at the time, so I took the initiative and went there on my own back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And when you went to the municipality, who did you confront?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: I stormed into the municipality building and where the president of the municipality usually is, and Deronjic was there and Kinez was there and Buco and Ljubo Simic and another man, I can't remember his name now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Kinez, that's his nickname?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, his name was Dragan Mirkovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And could you please tell us what happened when you stormed in there.

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: Well, anything could have happened, but luckily the worst didn't happen. I came in and said: "Who gave you the right, when you have other vehicles from the state enterprise, to take my vehicle that I saved up to buy and to provide me and my family with a livelihood? What gave you that right?"

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And what was their response?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: Well, this was their response: The gentleman, Mr. Buco, bashed his fist on the table and said: "We have to mobilise everything because it's a state of war, and we can mobilise what we like."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Buco is Mr. Davidovic?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: Davidovic, yes, that's right. He hit the table with his fist in demonstration and said: "Who are you? We have to mobilise."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did he tell you what the purpose for the mobilisation was, why they needed your transport vehicle?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: Well, he said that the people from Srebrenica, those ones, had to be driven to Kladanj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And what did you do after that?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: I had to agree to that because they said: "If you won't drive the vehicle, we have a driver and we'll let him drive it." And then I said to them: "Well, it's better for me to drive my own bus rather than somebody else who's going to -- who won't be so careful and might do anything to it." So that was it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And did you drive that bus?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you receive -- did you notify your commander at that point in time that you would be driving your bus for the next day or so?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you notify your commander when you were in Bratunac and your commander was up in the 2nd Battalion?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: I went back to the battalion and told the commander that my bus had been mobilised and I had to go with it. And he gave me permission.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Do you recall telling me something different yesterday when we were discussing this issue? That was: The day after you finished the driving is when you informed your battalion commander?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't really know whether it was that day, but anyway I had to inform the commander that I would be driving the bus.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I know that you had to inform him. The question is: Did you inform him before you started driving?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: No, no, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, in what condition was your bus?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: Relatively good condition.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did it need any repairs?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: Well, I did have something wrong with the pedal and there was some oil leakage from the oil tank and the clutch, something wrong there, so I had to keep putting in more motor oil.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you request any motor oil as a result of the leakage?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who did you request that from?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: I requested that from Loncarevic, what was his name? Pejo Loncarevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he with the Bratunac Brigade or was he with the municipality?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: It's the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And where was that in the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: By the hospital, there was a warehouse there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did you have to show them any documents in order to get the oil, or did you just show up and they automatically gave it to you?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: Well, I had the piece of paper for the car's requisitioning, nothing else. That's what I had, the requisition slip, but everybody knew that they had requisitioned my vehicle and I had to drive it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. All right. Now, could you please tell us -- incidentally, where was your bus located?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: It was at home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your home is where?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: Well, it's about 500 metres from the centre of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, if you could please tell us what did you do with your bus once you got the oil and you began driving it?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: When I had got the oil, I went to Potocari to load up the people who were there in Potocari.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, did anyone tell you --

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: Kladanj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone tell you to whom you were supposed to report once you got to Potocari?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: No, nobody told me anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you got to Potocari, did anyone tell you who was in charge?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: No, nobody told me anything. All I was told was to go to Potocari.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they ever mention Momir Nikolic, that he might be there coordinating all these activities and to check in with him?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: I saw him up there, but he didn't come up to me nor did I go up to him, because there were a number of buses there already. So we didn't have any communication.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Do you recall what he was doing when you saw him there?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: What was he doing? He was strutting around, because there was some blue helmets up there, so he would go to them and back. And he would communicate with them mostly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, when you got there, could you please explain to us exactly how the process worked.

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: When we came with the buses, we would make an about turn and there were soldiers from all parts, all kinds of soldiers. And we would make a turn there. And they would separate four or five buses and would the groups go in 50 or 60 people at a time, depending on the number of seats in the bus. They would load them up into the buses, and then they would make a column and we would go in single file or in column -- as a convoy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any soldiers kicking women or children or men into the buses?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any men being separated as they were trying to get on to the buses?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall approximately how many trips you took?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: Two -- I think it was twice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Could it have been three times? Three trips?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: Possibly, two or three times. I can't say exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, during those two to three trips, do you recall in your bus whether there were any men?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you tell us, if you recall now, their ages, the range of ages, of the men.

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: Well, they ranged from -- there was a young man, maybe 27, 30 years old, and then there were elderly people, too. 45, 50, that sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Incidentally, did you make any trips the next day, on the 13th?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: I didn't, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So on that particular day, could you please tell us how long it would take to make one trip to go there, come back, load up, and then go back out again. So how long would a trip take approximately?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: About two and a half hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And were there any soldiers in the bus when you were transporting the people?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you recall any incidents while you were taking the people from Potocari to Kladanj? Do you recall any incidents happening on the way there or once you got there?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: There was nothing on the way, but when we arrived there, when we got to Kladanj, there was some of those soldiers. And there was an incident with the young boy who was with me, and the soldiers took him away. I went up to them. They were a little insolent, and there was a captain there where we had to write down our names when we arrived and brought in those groups. We had to sign. I told him that permission had been given for him to pass through, so he ordered the soldiers to bring him back. And he went on with his father, and his father was in my bus, that young man's father.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So just to make sure that I understand everything, once you got to Kladanj to the border there where you were leaving -- letting the people out, you had to register?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, but I wasn't allowed to let the people out before I had registered with the captain, reported to the captain. And then I would open the door and they would step down in a column towards the crossing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Could you please describe to us this registration process and how did it work. You parked the car -- the bus, and then what?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. And then we would go to see the captain so that he could register us and have it down on paper that we had brought in the bus with the people at the border crossing at Kladanj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you have to record how many people you had transported, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it was basically you just going there, informing them of your name, your bus number --

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, and the number of the vehicle that had arrived.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Just incidentally, the day that you began driving these buses, the bus, was that the same day that you received notice that your bus had been mobilised?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: When Srebrenica fell, that's when it happened, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask the question again. I just want to make sure that we're correct. The day that you drove your bus, was that the same day that you received notice that your bus was mobilised and you went to the municipality?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Now, other than the one incident you just described to us, do you recall any other incidents with respect to transporting the people from Potocari to Kladanj?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, there were. There was one incident when I was stopped by the chief of police on my way back from Kladanj towards Bratunac, and he asked me to take a group of policemen up there because people had started looting those houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me stop you here. Where is "up there"?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: To Potocari, that's what I meant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were stopped in Bratunac and told to go to Potocari?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: That's how it was, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please continue.

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: And I took those policemen up there and returned. And then Josipovic said to me: "Would you please go because about 20 policemen" -- I don't know where they were from, Bijeljina, Zvornik, I don't know. They were still in Potocari and had to be transported to Bjelovac, because in the school probably --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me stop you here. We're going to go step by step. The first trip.

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're stopped by the chief of police and you're asked to go to Potocari with some police officers. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: To take them there, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now -- and who is the chief of police back then?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: Josipovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you recall how many police officers you took with you to Potocari?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: Not many. I think six or seven policemen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of those policemen?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether they were from Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: They weren't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They weren't or you don't know whether they were from Bratunac? Which of the two?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: I didn't know them. I didn't recognise them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. But it's possible that they could have been from Bratunac and you simply didn't recognise them. That's a possibility as well, no?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Now -- so you went -- so you took these individuals to Potocari. Right?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you wait for them or did you return right away to Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: I returned to Bratunac right away. And as I was approaching Bratunac, he asked me to go and fetch those policemen because a group of some 20 policemen had remained behind. That was probably a special unit. What do I know? And to transport them to Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, did you go back to Potocari?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you locate those police officers that you had to pick up?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did you locate -- were you able to find, on the road or on the side of the road, the police officers --

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: They were waiting for me on the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Could you please describe to us where on the road they were waiting for you.

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: They were waiting there where the civilians were on the road itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Was that beyond the yellow bridge, the checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. It was where the civilians were waiting for us to load them up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Do you recall approximately what time of day this would have been?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: In the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: Or early evening, or maybe it was about 4.00 p.m. I can't be precise about the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Now, what did you do once you picked them up -- well, first of all, did you recognise any of those police officers?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were they dressed?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: Camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I -- okay. But there were a lot of soldiers running around in camouflage uniforms. How did you know that those -- that was the group that you needed to pick up? How did you recognise them?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: Well, you recognise the police. They had the most freedom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, once you picked them up, where did you take them?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: I took them to Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And where is Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: Bjelovac is about 7 or 8 kilometres away from Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I don't recall whether I asked you. Do you know where they were from, these individuals? I know you didn't recognise them, but do you know where these police officers were from?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: I heard that they were special policemen from Bijeljina. I'm not sure, but that's what people said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, when you got to Bjelovac, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: Nothing. I set out. There was a big square area there, and I stopped there to let them out. And I saw that there was a bus there from a Srebrenica company from 1990 when that bus came along, and it was never registered until after the war. I was a little surprised when I saw that bus there. I wondered how it came to be there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let me stop you. What was the condition of the bus?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: It was brand new, brand new.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Even though you had seen it in 1990, it looked as if it had not been driven. Is that what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: It hadn't moved from the garage in Srebrenica or Potocari, rather.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And what were these -- did you recognise those police officers that were with this particular brand new bus that belonged, presumably, to the Srebrenica municipality?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. What were they doing with the bus?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: When I turned around and stopped behind it, they lifted the back and they were looking at it. And I got out and I said: "What's this bus doing here?" I thought it had brought someone there. And then one of them turned very insolently and spat at me and said: "That's none of your business." And I realised it was better for me to return to my bus, he might even have slapped me. So I went to our military police and reported to the duty officer to say that those people had taken the bus from Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let me stop you. Again, I want to go step by step. So after that incident you got in your bus and you left?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, where exactly did you go?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: In the direction of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And once you got to Bratunac, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: I went to the military police to report this incident concerning this bus.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And what were their response?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: They were insolent -- oh, you mean the military police? I misunderstood you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: Well, right away they sent a patrol up there. And later on I heard that there had been an incident because they wouldn't -- those policemen there wouldn't agree to hand over that bus. And then the civilian police got mixed up in it until that bus was confiscated from that special police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Is there any particular reason why you went to the Bratunac Brigade military police to report that and not to the civilian authorities, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: I was a mobilised soldier, and so of course I felt that I had to report this to the military police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, what happened after that? After you made that report to the military police, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: I personally?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: After reporting this to the police, I returned home. I told my wife that I was taking the bus to Ljubovija, to Serbia, Yugoslavia, because I said I would not give that bus up, that I would defend it with my life.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And why is that?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: Sir, it was my main source of income, of livelihood, that bus. I have nothing except that bus. If I had allowed it to be used, I would have been left without that bus.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Incidentally, during that day you told us you took two, perhaps three, trips and you went to -- and you made those other couple trips to Potocari that you told us about. Did you need to get gas for your bus, gasoline?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just so that we're clear, where did you get the gasoline from?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: I got the gasoline from the brigade, the command, from our military warehouse.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. That's the same place where you got the oil?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, the oil, too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, did you get permission from the assistant commander for rear services?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, from Loncarevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But wasn't the assistant commander Mr. Trisic?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Did you have to sign any documents that you were receiving this gasoline, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: I had to sign in a notebook. They wrote down how many litres they had given me, and then I had to sign for it. That's all that I had.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Incidentally, you said that you knew Mr. Blagojevic from growing up. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when he became the commander, did you have an opportunity to meet him, prior to this mobilisation of your bus, when he returned to Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, I would encounter him. But first of all I never imagined that he would requisition my bus. I was mobilised as a soldier, but I never thought they would requisition my bus.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, my next -- and that's my question. Once you saw that the civilian authorities were requisitioning your bus, why didn't you go and complain to Colonel Blagojevic to see if he could intervene?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: Well, he didn't have any power there, I'm sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. But did you ever make an attempt to meet with him?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. What did you do the following day?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: I returned up there to the command. When I left my bus there, I went back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when you say you left your bus there, you left your bus across the river, in Serbia. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then you returned to the 2nd Battalion?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir. I appreciate your honesty. And if you could please answer the questions of Mr. Stojanovic or the Prosecutor or the Judges, I would most appreciate it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Stojanovic, do you have any questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, Witness. We have no questions of this witness, bearing in mind his testimony today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Shin, some cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, we only have a few questions. Cross-examined by Mr. Shin:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Trisic.

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You explained just a little while back that you had informed the commander of the 2nd Battalion that you had -- your bus had been mobilised and you were going to go with your bus. Now, you also mentioned that the commander was a Mr. Stakic, but at one point he hadn't been there. Now, when you did inform your commander, was that Mr. Stakic or was that someone else?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: As Goran Stakic was away at the time, I informed Zoran Jovanovic, who was a security officer. And I said to him that I had to go because they wanted to requisition my bus. I would not allow anybody else to drive my bus. And he said he would inform the battalion commander of this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Zoran Jovanovic one -- as a security officer, was he part of this group of security officers that you were part of?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand. What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You had explained that you were part of a unit with seven other people that provided security for the battalion commands. Now, was he part of that security group?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What -- was he a military police officer?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: No. He was a security man.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For your battalion?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this was -- I think you explained that this was on the same day that you had been notified. You said that when you had been notified that you were -- that your bus had been mobilised, that you had gone to notify Mr. Jovanovic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: When they brought that piece of paper to me up there that my bus was to be requisitioned and that either I would drive it or they would find another driver for it, the commander wasn't there. So I said to Zoran: "Zoran, this is how things are: The bus is to be requisitioned. I have to go and get the bus." He said that he would transmit this message to the commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And when you say "up there," you mean this is the battalion command?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were there at the battalion command on duty, so you were there in your uniform at that time. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you also armed as a security officer, were you also armed?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: I wasn't an officer. I was only in charge of seven guards. I didn't have any rank. They were seven men unfit for military service, and when a civilian or an officer wanted to enter the command, they would have to go up and announce them. That's what we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you -- were you armed? Did you carry any side arms?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: No, no, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, who was it who told you that you should go to Potocari?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was the person who told you that you should go to Potocari with your bus?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: When I went to see about my bus and why it had been requisitioned, they said to me, Deronjic and Davidovic and those people, that the bus had to go to Potocari to transport the people from Potocari.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you got to Potocari, were there buses already there?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall how many buses were there already?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: There was a whole convoy, and I couldn't see. I didn't go out to count the buses, but there were many of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you recognise some of those other buses? Had you seen some of them before?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: There were buses from Vihor, from Zvornik, Drina, from all over the place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, we've heard that there were some buses in the Bratunac Brigade. Were there any buses from the Bratunac Brigade that you could recognise there at Potocari?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: You mean the Bratunac Brigade had buses?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I take it that means you don't know or do you know whether the Bratunac Brigade had buses?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: Just a moment. I didn't understand. What do you mean the Bratunac Brigade? The Bratunac Brigade, as a brigade, did not have a bus of its own. Vihor gave perhaps two buses for the use of the brigade, but the brigade as such did not own a bus.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware that the brigade had mobilised some buses prior to July 1995?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you were explaining the process of the loading of the passengers. You had explained to us that they were separating -- or permitting the buses in groups of five to six, and letting some 50 or 60 people through at a time. Would you explain to us who "they" are, who were these people who were separating these buses into groups of five or six?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: When we arrived to load up those people, the special police were there letting three, four, or five buses through at a time. And when they were loaded up, we would move forward. Then they would let some others go through and load up. And then we moved off in a convoy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any Bratunac Brigade military police officers at the buses?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, along the routes you passed through Konjevic Polje, is that correct, on your way to Kladanj?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall seeing a police checkpoint there?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You left in a group of five or six buses as well, is that correct, on your first trip, let's say?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Prior to arriving at that place in Kladanj where you had to register with that captain, did your convoy or any buses in your convoy stop at any time?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that -- would that be the same -- would the same be true of your other trips as well, whether it was one other trip or two other trips?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: No. There was always an escort. How then would they be able to stop us?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was your escort?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: There was always an escort in front. The first time, it included the UN, that vehicle. The second time, I think it was from that special unit, but there always had to be a car escorting us when we went.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, your bus, what was the make of your bus, manufacturer name?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: Dubrava, Dubrava Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What colour was your bus?

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: My bus had three colours: Yellow, blue, and white.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the registration number of your bus, if you can remember, the licence plate number.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A final few questions for you. I would like to ask you about the place where you picked up the oil and your fuel. Could you explain a little bit where that is within the Bratunac Brigade area.

utterances.speaker: RODOLJUB TRISIC
utterances.text: I don't know how well you know the area, but it was a shed, a wooden shed, near the health centre. That's where oil was stored, gasoline, and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: No further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any re-direct?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: At this stage, are there any documents to tender?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I guess there's none from the Prosecution's side either?

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: That's correct, there's nothing, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, Witness, thank you very much for coming to The Hague to give your evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: After the hearing is adjourned, Madam Usher will show you out of the room. Well, we'll have a break now and the next witness is waiting, I suppose?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, thank you. We'll have our break and we'll resume at 10.30.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas. Are you ready for your next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are there any protective measures?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: None, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we have the witness, please. Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, this witness has been identified as an executioner in this courtroom -- in the evidence in this courtroom by a 92 bis witness, just for his own rights.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If we could have the gentleman step out for a second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I take offence -- I take offence at the Prosecutor's language and the manner in which he stands up here grandstanding as if we the Defence don't know that individuals have rights and that we somehow failed to advise them of their rights. And I don't think it's proper the way he's grandstanding in front of the public.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, I think you have to regard the interventions by the Prosecution bona fide. At least this Bench did not know what the Prosecution said. I believe that the Prosecution has the obligation to inform us about any information concerning this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, this matter came up on Friday. At that point, I'll take them at their bona fides, as if we the Defence are totally ignorant about what it is to be a suspect. However, we did provide them with proofing notes. From reading the proofing notes, the Prosecution knows that the individual was told already that he has been fingered by one of their 92 bis witnesses. So it's more or less axiomatic that we as the Defence would have informed this individual of his rights. All I'm saying is that there is a better way of handling this, and I think the way in which it was done was offensive to the Defence. Because it demonstrates, or at least they are trying to demonstrate that we are derelict of our ethical obligations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Did you fulfill your obligations in this aspect?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, yes, I have. And we do it with every witness. We try to be very careful, we try to inform them of what the repercussions are, that even if they're not charged here that, you know there may be repercussions down the road. So we do that as a matter of right. One of the first things that we do when we do have a statement from the Prosecution, as we have in this particular case, because it's not merely that he's been fingered, but the Prosecution took a statement where it's very clear that the Prosecutor advised this individual of his rights, and he waived those rights and he gave a statement. It should also be noted from the proofing notes that this gentleman has cooperated both with the local police in Republika Srpska and has also provided testimony before a commission that's dealing with matters regarding Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. For your information, the Bench has not received your proofing notes at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we were told the preference would be to e-mail those proofing notes as opposed to faxing them. We faxed them last time and somehow there was -- we can do fax and e-mail as well. We apologise if you didn't get them, but it's my understanding that the proofing notes were e-mailed yesterday, sometime around 4.00 in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The problem with the fax is that it may be some leak out for some information. We did that just for the safety of the witnesses. Well, are you ready for your next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I am, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, could we have the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President and Your Honours. Examined by Mr. Karnavas:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what your name is.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: My name is Nenad Deronjic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you please tell us your last name letter by letter.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: D-e-r-o-n-j-i-c.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Mr. Deronjic. Could you please tell us what is your occupation today.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: I'm a policeman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where are you a police officer?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: In Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long have you been a police officer?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Since 1987.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I understand that in Bosnia and Herzegovina there was an UN organisation that was monitoring the police. Is that correct? The IPTF?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And am I correct in that there was a certification process of the police officers in part of the UN's effort to reorganise the -- and to reform the police force in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please tell us whether you had been recertified to be a police officer.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do have that certificate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, prior to coming here today, you have met with the Prosecution, have you not?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you gave a statement. Correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you had a copy of that statement, have you not?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it's -- at least the one that I have says that the statement was given on 12 March 2001. Would that be right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time that you gave that statement, did the Prosecution inform you of certain rights that you had because of a certain status that was designated to you?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall, sir, what status they told you that you had prior to the questioning process?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: I remember that they told me that I had the right to an attorney, that I had the right to remain silent, not to speak, and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that was because they considered you a suspect?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes, and it was stated that I was a suspect in the summons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And if my memory serves me correct, suspects in Bosnia and Herzegovina, under their current law, have to be warned of their rights as well, do they not?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And of course being a police officer, you know what it means to be a suspect?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, after you were told that you were a suspect by the Prosecution, did you give a statement?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did give a statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And since giving that statement, have you been questioned by anyone else?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us who has questioned you.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: I was questioned by an inspector of the CB of Bijeljina, pursuant to orders from the Prosecutor of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And who else has questioned you?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: I was also questioned by the inspector of the police station of Bratunac, Mr. Zivanovic, and that was pursuant to orders from the interstate commission for investigating the truth about Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Could you please tell us when it was, if you recall, that you gave these statements.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: I don't remember the exact date, but I do know that it was this year.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. 2004?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, before coming here today, were you advised by me of your current status, that is the status of a suspect?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you also not advised that you could, if you so chose, decline to answer any questions here in court, unless you were ordered to by the Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in spite of my warnings, are you still willing to testify here today?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am willing to testify.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us why you have come to testify here today, knowing that you have the status of suspect and knowing that the reason you have that status of suspect is because someone, a Prosecution witness, is accusing you in some executions.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: First of all, I have come here to testify because of the truth and also because of certain problems that I have been having with respect to that accusation or testimony by a certain individual who did what they did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, let's begin. You said that you became a police officer in 1987. Correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please tell us where you were serving back in 1987 when you began your career as a police officer.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: After I completed my police school, my first employment was at the police station of Gradacac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where is that located in comparison, say, to Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know how to explain it to you. It's approximately 170 kilometres or 180 kilometres from Bratunac on the road to Tuzla, closer to Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And how long were you a police officer there?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: I was a police officer there for four years.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after that, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: After that I went to the police station of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And what year was that, sir?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Is there a particular reason, sir, that in 1991 you were transferred to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: First and foremost, or rather, the first reason was nostalgia for my native town, because I lived in Bratunac which is a little way from Srebrenica and I wanted to be closer to home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So you are from Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, was there another reason why you made the transfer to Srebrenica, other than wanting to be close to Bratunac, where I assume you have family members?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Well, there's no specific reason, but I asked for Srebrenica, Bratunac, or Zvornik. The MUP okayed the Srebrenica posting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Which MUP would that be? Is that the Ministry of the Interior, but is there a particular centre that provided this transfer?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: The centre of the security services of Tuzla. That was the main centre for the region.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. How long were you a police officer in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: I worked in Srebrenica for barely a year.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then where did you go?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: I went to Bratunac, to the police station in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Were you transferred to Bratunac? Was that the reason?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you left, were Serb police officers still serving in the police station in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: There were Serbs who stayed on in Srebrenica, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, once you moved to Bratunac, since that point in time, have you been a police officer anywhere else?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And so currently you are still a police officer for the Bratunac municipality?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you started your career as a police officer. Have you moved up to the level of inspector or any other position?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So would it be fair to say that today you are dressed in a police uniform and you are patrolling the streets as a police officer?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's just how it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I want to focus your attention to July 1995. Okay. And as a reference point, I'm going to choose July 11, 1995, because that -- we know that on that particular day, Srebrenica fell. Okay?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do you recall, sir, where you were on that particular day?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: On that particular day I was at the control point at Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. When you say "control point" or the checkpoint, I take it, how many police officers were there?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: At the checkpoint, depending on the situation, there were at least two policemen, sometimes more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were the policemen from?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Those policemen were from the police station of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know, sir, if you and the other policemen that served at that checkpoint had been subordinated to and were working under or for the Bratunac Brigade when you were at that particular location?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: No. They didn't have any role there, anything to do with the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us, based on your recollection, how long that checkpoint existed prior to the fall of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, but it was there for a long time. I don't know exactly how long, but a long time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When we say "a long time," are we speaking weeks? Months? Years?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Well, years.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, prior to that occasion on July 11, 1995, when you were serving there at that checkpoint, had you been to that checkpoint before?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes, often. I was often at that checkpoint and I was scheduled there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. First, tell us: What was the purpose and function of that checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: The purpose of that checkpoint was to control the comings and goings, transport traffic, transport of goods, that kind of thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. May I ask how you were armed when you were at that checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: We had side arms, pistols, and automatic rifles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And how were you dressed when you were at that checkpoint, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: At the checkpoint, we were dressed in blue camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And so I take it if someone were to go to that checkpoint, they could visibly notice that you were a member of the MUP, as opposed to being with the military?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, could you tell us, please, to the best of your recollection, what sort of shifts did you have when you were at that checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: At the checkpoint we frequently had 24-hour shifts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, if it was a 24-hour shift, surely you would need some period of time to rest. Were there any facilities or any means for which to catch some sleep if one needed any?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes. At the checkpoint there was a police container with beds for rest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Was there any jail facilities at that checkpoint? In the event you needed to detain someone and lock them up, were there any facilities available?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what the communications means were.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: In the official premises, there was a fixed radio station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was it -- how -- with whom was it connected?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: It was connected with the base, that is to say with the police station at Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the Bratunac Brigade headquarters? Were you connected with them through this communication means?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Hypothetically speaking, if there was an occasion where you needed to communicate with the Bratunac Brigade from that location, since you were not directly linked, could you please tell us how that would have been done.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: That would have been done in the following way: We would have called up the police station at Bratunac, and then they would have contacted the Bratunac Brigade and its command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, you indicated that there were these 24-hour shifts in general. Could you please tell us: What was the method of being assigned to the checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Well, there wasn't any special method. A schedule for the services in the police station would be drawn up, and that's how we were deployed to the checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who would make up the schedule deploying individual police officers to the checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: The schedule or duty roster was compiled by the workers in the police station and Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. At that point in time, sir, who was the individual or individuals, if you are aware of, that kept track of those records?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: The deputy commander, Dragan Nedeljkovic, the deputy, Slavoljub Tesic, and Slavoljub Mladjenovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So I take it there was a logbook being kept?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before coming here today, did you have a chance to look at that logbook?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before meeting with the Prosecution back in 2001, March 12th, did you have a chance to look at that logbook?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you please tell us where that logbook is kept.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: That logbook was kept with the deputy komandir Dragan Nedeljkovic in a safe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were you able to look at that logbook if it was kept in a safe?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: I would ask the deputy komandir, Dragan Nedeljkovic, to give me the logbook to take a look.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, when you looked at it, were you alone or was Mr. Nedeljkovic there as well, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nedeljkovic was present as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you by any chance alter the logbook to insert your name in any place or to erase your name in any places to cover up any activities that you might have been involved in during the critical period, which is July 11, say, to July 20th, 1995?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you met with the Prosecution, did you inform them, if you recall, of the existence of this particular logbook that would reflect your whereabouts on specific days or your duties, the functions which you were carrying out at the time?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Aside from this particular logbook, are there any other records kept that you are aware of?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: At the moment, I don't know that there is; however, there were patrol orders for the duties we performed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And where were those patrol orders kept?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: The patrol orders were archived, but I don't know whether they have been destroyed or not. They were archived in the police station in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you check by any chance the archives to see whether the patrol orders are available today?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: I did try to check, and I think they're missing. Most probably, they've been destroyed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, the Bratunac police department was part of the Zvornik centre, was it not?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you by any chance check with Zvornik, the centre, to see whether any records exist there that might also help us here today?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now, let me show you what has been marked -- well, before we do that, before we do that, let's talk a little bit about -- let's go through the chronology of the events. You indicated that you were at the checkpoint on July 11, 1995. Could you please tell us where you were the next day, July 12th, 1995, if you recall.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: On the next day, the 12th of July, I was in Bratunac for a period of time and after that in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us at what time or on which day you left the checkpoint at Konjevic Polje to go to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: I left the checkpoint in Konjevic Polje at 0800 hours on the 12th of July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That would be 8.00 in the morning. Right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, was that the normal time period when there would be a change in shift, or was this some sort of a special occasion that you left at 8.00 that particular morning?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes. This was the usual time when shifts changed at the checkpoint in Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please tell us, if you recall, how you left or how you got to Bratunac from Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: I can't say exactly which vehicle it was. We had a Golf, an official vehicle, and a Land Rover. I used one of those two vehicles to go to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, when you got to Bratunac, could you please tell us what you did.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: When I got to Bratunac, I reported to the police station in Bratunac. I handed over the official order I had, on the basis of which I had worked, and I was told by the duty officer that due to the newly arisen situation in Srebrenica, I was to be on standby.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, when you were on standby, where were you standing by? Did you go home? Were you in the station? Did you walk around, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: For a brief period of time, I was in the police station. And then acting on orders, I went to the main crossroads in order to regulate the traffic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "the main crossroads," what are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: When we say "the main crossroads," we mean the one near the Fontana Hotel where the Srebrenica/Konjevic Polje roads are joined up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That rather busy intersection with the bend?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you recall how you were dressed then?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: I was wearing a blue camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Was there anyone else at that intersection when you were there controlling the traffic, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: I don't recall exactly, but I assume there was somebody else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you recall how long you were at that intersection controlling the traffic?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: I don't recall exactly how long it was, but it was until the afternoon, around 1500 hours, that I stayed in that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And where did you go after 1500 hours?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: After 1500 hours we went, acting on orders, in the direction of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me stop you here. When you say "we," who is "we"?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: "We" means members of the 2nd Company of the special unit of the police of the Zvornik public security station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So in addition to being identified as a member of the Bratunac Brigade -- Bratunac police department, am I to understand you were also -- or inclusive of that, you were a member of the 2nd Company?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I take it you had been a member of the 2nd Company prior to that particular moment when you were told to go towards Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you recall about what time it was that you and the others went to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: I can't tell you the exact time, but it was around 1500 or 1600 hours in the afternoon.
