utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us, to the best of your recollection, how many of your were there when you went to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly how many members there were. This can be established, but there were two buses and several passenger vehicles or cars.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, was everybody in the 2nd Company from Bratunac or were they from other areas as well?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: No. They were from other areas as well in the area covered by the Zvornik centre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Could you please tell us, if you recall, who was in charge. Who was the komandir.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: You mean the 2nd Company?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the 2nd Company.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: The komandir of the 2nd Company of the special police unit was Slavoljub Mladjenovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if this gentleman was with you on that day when you went to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there another komandir for the other units, if you know, that went with you to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: I know only that the chief of the public security station in Srebrenica, Petko Pavlovic, was there. There weren't any other komandirs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Could you please tell us who then would have been overall in charge of the MUP that had gone to Srebrenica. Was there one person who was in charge of the various MUP that were there?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I only know about the 2nd Company of the special police unit. I only know about that unit, who the komandir was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. How long did you stay in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: As a member of the 2nd Company, I stayed there for seven or eight days. I think it was eight days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, the day that you got there - which, if I have the date right, is 12 July, 1995 - what exactly did you do?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: First of all, on our arrival in Srebrenica, we came to the front of the police station, where we worked on setting up the police station in Srebrenica, and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you know whether patrols were set up to walk around Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes, patrols were set up and so were checkpoints.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall -- well, let me ask you: Did you go on any patrols? Did you walk around?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes. From time to time, I did, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall whether anybody was left behind, any of the Muslim residents of Srebrenica were still there when you and the others arrived?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes. There was a small number of elderly people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Could you please tell us what happened to them, if you know.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: They were mainly in front of their houses next to the road, and as far as I know there was some vehicles that they got into working order. And then they drove them off to Potocari.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, who's "they"? Who drove them off to Potocari?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: It was the working unit that drove them to Potocari. That was the name of the group. They were to get certain vehicles into working order and then transport those people to Potocari.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any dead bodies lying around the streets of Srebrenica when you were patrolling?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if any were found or seen by others?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: I don't know. According to what I heard later, people did say that they had seen some bodies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So while you didn't see any yourself, you heard that others had seen some bodies?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And do you know what might have happened to those bodies?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. We talked about July 12th. Could you please tell us what you did the rest of the days. You were there for approximately eight days, you indicated. Could you please give us a general impression of what you did for the other days.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: First of all, as a policeman who worked in Srebrenica before the war, I was duty officer in the police station in Srebrenica. I also worked on the checkpoints in the direction of Zeleni Jadar, the checkpoint near Domavija, and occasionally I patrolled the town. And that was it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, how was it that you stayed so long there? Is there any particular reason, if you know?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During that eight-day period, where were you sleeping?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: During that eight-day period, we had rooms that we had arranged in the police station, and we had rooms in the Srebrenica police station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever leave Srebrenica during those days?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One detail I wanted to backtrack on. You told us that you went there on the 12th. Could you please describe to us how you got there, what route you took to get to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: We went to Srebrenica along the road from Bjelovac to Sase, Zalazje and then on to Srebrenica, the playing field, and then on to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I take it you did not go through Potocari?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Incidentally, did you ever go to Potocari on that day or the following day, the 12th and 13th, you yourself?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: No. In that period, I did not go toward Potocari at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During that eight-day period when you were in Srebrenica from the 12th onwards, could you please tell us whether you ever left Srebrenica to go anywhere else.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you met with the Prosecution, did they inform you that you had been named by a witness as having taken part in certain executions?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: They didn't inform me about that, but I can clarify.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: They only told me that a certain person had said that I had been seen in Konjevic Polje in that period of time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, before coming here today, you had an opportunity to hear what this witness testified to during the Krstic case, did you not?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you heard where this individual -- and I'm speaking of this -- this has come in under 92 bis as P797. You heard where this individual places you at a particular date and time at certain executions that occurred in I believe it's Jadar River. Correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now -- and this witness, who incidentally is identified as Witness S, indicated certain things, including that you were part of an execution squad. Concretely speaking, and I want you to look at the Honourable Members of this Trial Chamber, look them in the eye and tell them: Did you participate in those events which Witness S has identified you as being part of? Please look at the Honourable Members of the Trial Chamber and tell them whether you have participated in those events.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: No, I did not participate in those events.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you in that area on the 12th or the 13th or the 14th of July?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: No, I was not in that area in this period.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That area where the witness, Witness S, places you, is that near Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: What area do you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you heard where -- and I even showed you the pictures, where allegedly this individual was initially picked up and where they take them -- where they took them. That would have been at or near the intersection of Konjevic Polje. Correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And you do not deny being at that intersection on July 11th. Correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: I do not deny it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. But what you're telling us here is on the morning of the 12th at 8.00, you left there shortly after that day, went to Srebrenica, and at no time on the 12th, 13th, 14th, 15th, 16th, 17th, 18th, 19th, 20th, you returned to that area. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection, leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. You may put your question another way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever return to that area during the period of time in which I just noted in the previous question?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: No, I did not return in that period.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And did you tell that to the Prosecutors when they came calling on you in 2001?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now -- incidentally, before I show you this, could you please tell us whether you participated in any atrocities at any point in time during this critical period?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: No, I did not participate in any atrocities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you ever told of the identity of Witness S?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Nobody ever told me the name of that witness, and I don't know who the witness is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us then why would this unknown witness to you, why would he specifically name you as being at that location, committing those atrocities on that particular day, assuming that that's when those atrocities occurred there.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: I really don't know for what reasons that witness named me. I don't even know who the witness is or anything about him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, let me show you what has been marked for identification purposes as Defence Exhibit D124.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I believe I provided the large copies for everyone. And we can even put one on the ELMO. I don't know how successful that would be. It's not necessary, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I don't think it's necessary, since everybody has got a copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If -- do you see -- first of all, do you know -- do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How is it that you recognise it?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: I recognise it because I had occasion to come across this document before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please tell us where this document is from.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: This document is from the duty roster by the assistant, Nedeljkovic, Dragan, it's from his book.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is that the same book that you told us was pulled out of the safe for you to look at in front of him?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The same book that you informed the Prosecution that they could go look for if they so wanted to look for the records?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, is -- obviously this is a copy of that page, is it not?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, is this copy a fair and accurate representation of what is in that logbook?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, it's a fair copy and an accurate copy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Could you please tell us what dates are reflected on this particular page of the logbook.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: On this page of the logbook, the month of July 1995 is reflected and all the days of that month.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, how do we know that it's July 1995? What is it that tells us that this page reflects that particular month? Is there anything on this that would give us that clue?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Well, it says here: "July 1995".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you please tell us on which corner of this document that is located.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: It's at the top, in the top left-hand corner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Is that your handwriting, sir?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that mark was there on the original logbook when it was copied. Correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see your name anywhere on this page?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do see it, under number 36.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us whose handwriting that is.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: It's the handwriting of the deputy komandir, Dragan Nedeljkovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. It's a little difficult to read this, but what I would like you to do is please explain to us some of the different initials that we see on this particular document.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Very well. From the first day of July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: On the 1st of July I was PR, that is to say standby.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So what does standby -- we're going to go step by step. So when it says "PR," which means standby, what does that include? What are your functions when you are standing by?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: When we are standbys, it means that movement would be imminent, and we were standbys either at the police station or we were placed on standby at home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And how many days are you standby?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: On the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd of July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. What about the 4th of July? What are you doing?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: On the 4th of July was the service of patrolling around town from 2200 to 0600 hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how do we know that?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: We know that because it says "P," which is underlined.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what does P stand for?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: P is Pozorna, which is guard service.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Guard service. Okay. What about the next day?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: The next day is the 5th and it says 0600 hours, which means that I left the night shift and I was off that day, I had a free day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. What about the 7th -- or the 6th -- the 6th?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: The 6th was PR again, which means standby.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Incidentally, do you recall where you were standing by on this day?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But would it be fair to say that when you're standing by you're in Bratunac, not in Konjevic Polje or some other location?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes, in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, what about the next day, the 7th?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: On the 7th of July I was at the checkpoint at Konjevic Polje from 0800 hours to 0800 hours, which means 24 hours around the clock.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, how do we know that you were at Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: We had the initials KP, Konjevic Polje, the time from when to when, and the time spent at the checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, we see in that box it says 08 to 08, and underneath it I believe I see a 24. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the 24 means 24 hours?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: 24 hours of service, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, if we go to the 8th, what does that say?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: For the 8th it says "08 hours," which means I left the night shift and was off that day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do we know you were off that day? What tells us that that's an off day?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Well, according to this schedule, it says "08," which means I was on duty during the night, and I had the next day to rest up because I was on night duty, night shift.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. We go to the 9th then. What is that?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: The 9th also says "PR" or standby.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The 10th?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: The 10th, Konjevic Polje from 08 hours to 08 hours, 24 hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And then the 11th. On the 11th, also Konjevic Polje from 08 to 08 hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So the 08, the second 08, that would be 08, the 12th of July. Correct? So you're from 8.00 in the morning of the 11th to 8.00 in the morning of the 12th?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: From 8.00 in the morning of the 11th to 8.00 in the morning of the 12th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, let's go to the 12th. What do we see here?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: It says here: "08 hours," which means that I worked the night shift. And we would regularly have gone off-duty. But it says BD, which is combat activity, which means that a police company was engaged.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters note that the P for Pozorna service was beat or patrol duty, earlier on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, combat duty, I want to talk about that a little bit. What are the initials, first of all, that tells us that it's combat duty?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: The abbreviation which tells us it was combat activity was BD.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: BD. Now, how many days do we have for BD after the initial one, which is on the 12th?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: We have nine days, but may I be allowed to count them?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Go for it. Certainly.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Nine days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And it's during this period of time that you've told us that you were in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do we know that the BD, combat duty, doesn't mean that you were sent out into the woods to hunt down people so that you could execute them, as the witness has suggested, and as the Prosecution believes?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It's leading. It's talking about the belief of the Prosecution; that's not relevant. Ask him a non-leading question, I wouldn't object, especially on this topic, when the document appears the way it appears.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, I think the last phrase is quite unnecessary, to mention the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. I'll withdraw.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please rephrase your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do we know that this BD, that says combat duty, that you were doing something other than being in Srebrenica? How do we know that?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: We know that by the fact that the 2nd Company was engaged at that place, and I was a member of the 2nd Company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And I take it if we were to contact some of the other individuals in -- that you claim, that you claim, were in Srebrenica at the time that you went, they might also be able to tell us whether you were there with them?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Or they might tell us that you were not with them. They would be able to verify one way or the other whether you're telling us the truth here today?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes, you can verify that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And just so we are absolutely clear, to the best of your recollection when you went to Srebrenica on that mission, starting on the afternoon of July 12th, who was your komandir, your commanding officer, at that time for that particular mission?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: At that time, on that mission, it was Company Commander Slavoljub Mladjenovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And may I ask: Where is that gentleman located today?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Slavoljub Mladjenovic is located today in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't recall right now whether you mentioned this name to the Prosecution when they were interviewing. Having read your statement, do you recall whether you informed them who your commanding officer was at that point in time, in the event they wanted to take the trouble to go to Bratunac to meet with this individual and talk to them?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did tell them who the commanding officer of the 2nd Company was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: At this point in time, Your Honour, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Deronjic. You will be questioned by Mr. Stojanovic, perhaps, the Prosecutor, the Judges. I would most appreciate it if you would be as honest and forthright with them as you were with me. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Karnavas. We'll sit until 12.00 sharp. Mr. Stojanovic, do you have any questions to this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. In view of our position, it is clear that we do not have any questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Cross-examined by Mr. McCloskey:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning. Can you first of all tell us a little bit more about the 2nd Company. Is -- for example, is that known as the 2nd Company of PJP from Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is the 2nd Company of the PJP from Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is that one of several companies that are organised out of Zvornik of police officers to take part in combat duties when necessary -- or other duties at some times?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For example, I think it was the 6th Company which had several men stationed at Konjevic Polje in this period up -- leading up to the fall of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the 6th Company was mostly older men. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it true that the companies were divided like from 1 to 6, and that the 1st Company and the 2nd Company were the more fit, younger, military-able men?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as you've said, your company, the 2nd Company, that was made up of people all over the -- from the Zvornik municipality?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in -- for that period of July 1995, can you tell us roughly how many men would have been on the duty roster for the 2nd Company.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know the exact number of the members from the 2nd Company from Bratunac, but there might have been seven or eight deployed at -- amongst the police stations of the centre. And then we can learn the number that way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But about how many total from the other police centres? I think you've mentioned some of the Milici, Skelani, Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Milici, Skelani, Vlasenica, Zvornik, Sekovici. I don't know exactly, but seven or eight people from the police station from the members of the other -- of the 2nd Company. So if you multiply that number with the police stations, that would give you the total.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So about five police stations, seven or eight people per station. 35, 40, something like that?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you know most of the people that were on the 2nd Company?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: I knew all the members from the Bratunac police station, and I also knew some people from other police stations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know most of the people from the other police stations, at least by sight, that was on the 2nd Company?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly, but yes, I did know -- well, not a lot of people, but ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You did know them?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: I knew them, but superficially. I didn't know them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Were -- all the unit commanders for the 2nd Company, you've already mentioned them?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes. I knew the commanding officer of the 2nd Company personally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any other commanders for July 1995 besides I think it's Mladjenovic?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: There was just his deputy, the deputy company commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you mentioned his name as well?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: No, I don't think I mentioned his name. But if you want me to give you the name of the deputy, I can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Goran Djelemic, I think it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where was Mr. Djelemic on the 12th, 13th, 14th of July?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: I don't know where he was. All I said was that he was the deputy, the deputy of Slavoljub Mladjenovic, but I can't remember whether he was up there with us at Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I just want to ask you to help us -- there's an English language translation that doesn't fit B/C/S very well. So I want to ask you about that a little bit. Sometimes your PJP company gets referred to as a special police company. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: No, that's not right. Our company's name was special -- or special police unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. That's the problem. It's this special police unit, and it's not your problem. It's an English/B/C/S problem. Can you distinguish your unit that you've talked to from the, for example, the 2nd Sekovici Detachment of the special police? Are they two different things, your 2nd Company and the 2nd Sekovici Detachment of the special police?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: They were two quite different units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. The 2nd Sekovici Detachment was under Mr. Borovcanin. And you were basically under Dragomir Vasic from the CSB Zvornik. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes. The main chief of the centre of the public security centre Zvornik was Dragomir Vasic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if the 1st PJP unit was assigned to work under the command of Mr. Borovcanin around this time period, 11, 12 July?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, when you were -- when did you first start hearing about getting organised as a -- as the 2nd Company of the PJP, as opposed to being an individual police officer that had been assigned to the Konjevic Polje checkpoint? When did you first hear that you were going to be -- your 2nd Company PJP unit was getting organised?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: I don't know the exact date. However, in that organisation and establishment of the PJP company, I took part. I didn't organise it, but I was present when those companies were established.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I mean is: Specifically you have described yourself, I believe, as on the morning of the 12th of July you wake up, I believe, as a Bratunac police officer about ready to get off your assignment at Konjevic Polje, and then you've testified that you went to Srebrenica later that day as part of the 2nd Company PJP. So is that correct? Or were you in Konjevic Polje as part of the 2nd Company?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: No. The 2nd Company and all the other companies were activated in certain situations and at certain periods.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. So you were not a member of the -- you were not an activated member of the 2nd Company while you were in Konjevic Polje on the 12th. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes. I performed police duties, which means duties from the police domain at Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when did you first hear that you were going to be activated as a member of the 2nd Company?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: For the July period or before?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For that July 11th, 12th period. Did they tell you on the 11th, the next day you were going to be a -- the 2nd Company was getting together? Or did you not hear until the 12th?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: I heard about that on the 12th of July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what time?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Well, I think it was around 12.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From who?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: I can't remember who said that, but it could have been the duty officer. It could have been the police duty officer, or it could have been the -- any of the chiefs who were at the premises of the Bratunac police station. It could have been any of those.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the group that went down to Srebrenica, was this that 35, 40 people that you have talked about from the different areas, including Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any part of the 2nd Company that was sent somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: I don't know about that, but I don't think so. I don't think anybody was sent somewhere else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, on the afternoon/evening hours of the 12th of July, Muslims from Srebrenica, armed Muslims, were breaking through the area around Konjevic Polje, and that was a combat zone. Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you're aware that Konjevic Polje has become a combat zone shortly after the time that you left it. So you must have been relieved to have been able to get the assignment to go down to Srebrenica, which was not a combat zone?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: You could put it that way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were any of your colleagues so unlucky that they got assigned to go to the combat zone, Konjevic Polje, Ravni Buljim, Cerska?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: I don't know about that. I know that they were at Konjevic Polje, that that's where the 6th Company was. Now, as to the rest, to the other areas, I don't know if anybody went.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I'm talking about the 2nd Company, your crew. You would have known if they had been in the combat -- if some of them would have gotten sent to combat, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: No, no. Those of us who went up there, they didn't send us to any other places except to the area around the town of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in this --

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Can I have some water, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please. Any time you need water. And in this document that you brought us this copy of, it was Exhibit 124, sorry. From 12 July through about 20 July, it says BD, which means combat activities. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've earlier described that your activities in Srebrenica were patrolling the streets, staying at checkpoints. So are you suggesting that combat activities is what you were doing in Srebrenica when you were patrolling the streets and manning a checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Well, you know what, this activation of the 2nd Company in itself, regardless of which area you would go and what you would do, that in our logbook, in our daily logbook, would be written down and recorded as BD, as combat activity. They couldn't write down beat duty or patrol duty because we were already members of the 2nd Company. So they couldn't write down "Pozorna Sluzba".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's see what they did write down. From 21 July through about 29 July, my translation says "SJB Srebrenica." Is that correct? So by this document you're not doing SJB Srebrenica until 21 July. And before that, you're doing combat duties.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes. However -- may I be allowed to explain, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Always.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: On that date I moved to work as a police officer in the Srebrenica police station, because I -- that's the area I worked in before the war. And the order, from the chief of the public security centre, was any old policeman who had worked before the war, should move to Srebrenica to work in the police there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's your explanation for this?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you want to break at 12.00 noon, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Is this a good time for the break?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It's as good as any. I shouldn't be, hopefully, too long. I should be able to finish certainly today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll have a break and we'll resume at 12.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I want to show you a logbook that you might be able to help us identify. You may or may not recognise it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And for Your Honours, the photocopy of the book is 847. And we have a partial English translation. We have it for the 12th of July and for the 14th of July. Unfortunately, there was some complications with the 13th of July, but I think the witness should be able to help us with that. And if I could just -- I also brought in the original book that we have. If we could show the original to the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if you could just take the book.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And if we could get the English for the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And first, before opening the book, can you just read us what the front of the actual original book says.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: "Duty roster, Srebrenica SV, of the 12th of July, 1995."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you seen this book before today?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: I don't remember having seen it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You had mentioned a document. I think you called it patrol record or something. Is this it or is this something different?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: This is the duty roster in the Srebrenica public security station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that different than the record you told Mr. Karnavas about when you said that there should be another record that might help us out?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: I said there might be patrol orders. That's an order you get when you set out on a patrol, and you always carry it with you. When you complete your patrol, you fill in the form and hand it in at the police station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's the order you told us about that you handed in on the morning of the 12th in the Bratunac police station?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you find that order when you were looking for records?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't find it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, if you could just help us with this book. This hopefully won't take long. If you could just open up the next page and tell us what's in that, if it's anything significant. I just want to understand. What does that next page say?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: On the next page it says: "Duty roster book."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So it's just a repeat of what was on the cover?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So then let's go to the next page, and I think that's the next page we have the actual translation for. And we see that it says "12 July," and it lists various things, which unfortunately -- "work in the police station," various other duties. Do you see your name for 12 July?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's under what is the title "sector 1"?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, sector 1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was sector 1 at the time?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: I don't know, but I think it was the Domavija hotel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, could you go to the next time you see your name. I believe it's 13 July, and unfortunately the English -- we didn't get an English of 13 July. Do you find 13 July in the book?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where is your first name -- where is your name first noted?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: My name is noted 13th July, 1995, duty service from 19 to 07.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where is that service?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: In the police station in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is that 1900 hours?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: 1900 hours in the evening until 0700 hours in the morning of the next day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that's 7.00 p.m., 13 July, to the morning of 14 July?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think there's another reference on 13 July for your name. Could you take a look further in the book -- on the 13th. It may be the next page. Do you see yourself again?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do, under number 1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is number 1?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: This is just a list with ordinal numbers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is there a heading where your assignment was above your name?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: The title is: "Security Domavija Drina."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that may be on page 5 of the English translation. Unfortunately the translation just left off the fact that this came under the heading of 13 July in the book. And what are the hours that you're listed for the Domavija hotel?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Security of Domavija/Drina from 07 to 19.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do you have any recollection of where you were actually working on the 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly, but if it says here that it was Domavija, I think we were up there by the Domavija Hotel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, according to the record you last read out to us it was 0700 hours to 1900 hours at the hotel. And then the first record you read to us from the 13th was from 1900 hours to the following morning. So did you work that long?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: I was able to work that long because at the police station in the duty service we had beds and we could have a rest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you resting, which one of these 12-hour periods?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: You mean in the police station?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Do you know when you took your rest on the 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: On the 13th of July, I could have taken a rest from 1900 to 0700 hours in the police station during my shift of duty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And if you could look just closer at that -- the Domavija Hotel entry next to your name where it says 0700 to 1900. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does it look like someone has marked over and changed the numbers there with a pen?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: There are some indications, but I think somebody must have made an error. Maybe they wanted to state a different time. Yes, but it does seem to have been changed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Nobody else is changed on that day, is it?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: No, no one else is changed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much. Now, I want to show you a document that's been marked as P665. It's in evidence in this case. And you've earlier told us that Dragomir Vasic was the boss of CSB Zvornik. And I've got a copy of the B/C/S for you to take a look at, 665B. It's not easy to read, but it's readable. And this is a report about some -- the activities dated 12 July. And I'll just go over it a bit with you. Most of the early parts where it talks about General Mladic and a meeting we don't need to talk about. It talks about some of the events in Potocari. And then on paragraph 5 it says: "Acting upon the -- President Karadzic's order, which conveyed to us today over the phone, the 2nd Company of the Zvornik PJP, two platoons, 60 men, shall be dispatched to Srebrenica with a task to secure all facilities of vital importance in the town, at all costs, and protect them from looting and misappropriation." So is that your unit?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were there two platoons, like it says here?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: I think there were two platoons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. It goes on to say: "It will carry out the task without cooperation of military police which is busy with other tasks." Is that correct? You didn't have any MPs down there in Srebrenica with you?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: No, we didn't have any, so it's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is a platoon about 30 men?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Approximately, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. The last line says: "A platoon of this company will lie in ambush at Ravni Buljim, since the Muslim groups were spotted fleeing along this axis." You know where Ravni Buljim is, I take it?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And we had talked about the combat area around Konjevic Polje, Ravni Buljim. This Ravni Buljim is the area where the combat with the Muslims is taking place on 12 and 13 July, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you part of the platoon from your company that was in ambush at Ravni Buljim?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: No, and I don't even know whether that platoon went to that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said earlier that you know most of the people in your platoon -- in your company. And given the combat that was going in that area, if they had been there, I'm sure you would have heard something about it, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: While we were up there, I didn't hear about it. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Let me show you another document. This has been marked Exhibit 848. And it's a document -- if we could put the English on the ELMO, the front page. It's got a title on it: "Republika Srpska, Ministry of the Interior, public security centre, Zvornik." 12 July, the date. And it says -- it's entitled "Bulletin." Can you put the B/C/S version on the ELMO so the Court can see what you're seeing. Now, first of all, can you tell us what a bulletin is that would come from -- this is Rodoljub Vidakovic, the operations duty officer for that day. Can you just briefly tell us what the operations duty officer's reports or bulletins are, if you know.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: The bulletins, as far as I know, are reports by certain persons who can submit their report to someone. So it's a kind of report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And this handscratching on the front of it, do you recognise that handscratching or can you offer an opinion of what it might be?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's a compound question. We can take it step by step, because he's also asking in the second part of the question, this compound question, to guess or to offer some sort of a speculative opinion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Let's go step by step.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise the handwriting?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you ever been the duty officer writing bulletins like this?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: We didn't write bulletins like this, but we wrote similar sorts of reports. I don't know what this bulletin is about, because I haven't read it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you give us your opinion on what these handwritten remarks might be.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: No, I have no idea what they might mean. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let's go over just some of the information. Maybe we can help. In the right corner it says: "Konjevic Polje, 2nd Company." And underneath it says: "Sandici, 1st Company." Now, did you know on the 12th of July where the 1st Company of the PJP Zvornik was?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know that on the 13th of July the 1st Company of the PJP Zvornik was actually in Sandici on a video?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I don't mean to be disruptive here, but it would appear that counsel is testifying now. First he testified as to what's on this document, as opposed to allowing the gentleman to identify what's in it. And now he appears to be testifying, giving testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think the witness said that he didn't know that in all the way. So what's the problem? I don't see any problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There's a famous video that people have been watching for years and years of the road between Konjevic Polje and Bratunac. Have you seen parts of that video?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: I didn't have an opportunity of seeing this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. It says: "A K-9 unit in Liplje." Liplje, we know, is a little south than Zvornik. Was there in the CSB Zvornik or one of the police stations a dog or some kind of a dog unit?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, there was no such unit during the war, in the police stations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And as we go down it says: "IV Srebrenica," and then under that is: "2nd Company." And then there's numbers underneath there. Do you know what IV Srebrenica is. I think it's roman numeral, Srebrenica. Yeah, IV, Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Believe me, I don't know. I assume the 2nd Company was planned for Srebrenica or something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And just as we go on later on the next page under combat activities it -- if you could just take a look at the next page. It talks about some of the companies, but your company is not mentioned here. But it does say: "The 6th Company, PJP, was in the area Konjevic Polje," like you've told us, "as well as Han Pogled." Where is Han Pogled?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Han Pogled overlooks Vlasenica. It's above Vlasenica in the direction of Han Pijesak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So a good distance away from the Srebrenica event.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, we have just I think one more. It's 849. It's another bulletin. And if we could put the English on the front page and give you a chance to see the B/C/S. The operations duty officer that day was Vlado Kovacevic. It's dated 14 July. If we could put the front of the -- or the title page on the ELMO. Under the bulletin it says: "Bulletin of daily events of the Zvornik public security centre for 13/14 July." So it starts out with paragraph 1: "Combat activities." Unfortunately there had been some men killed. Then there's some typical criminal events. There may be, perhaps, some looting. And law and order and traffic. Various, it looks like, police tasks. But if you could take a little closer look at paragraph 5: "Other business." "Due to infiltration of enemy military formations from Srebrenica into the zone of Zvornik CJB and areas of Konjevic Polje, Cerska, Han Pogled, Dzafin Kamen, Snagovo, Maricici, and other places at risk, the 1st, 2nd, 5th, and 6th Companies of the Zvornik CJB are engaged. In coordinated action with the police from Doboj, Bijeljina, and Pale, as well as the VRS, they are laying ambushes." Did you and your group get called out of Srebrenica to go coordinate and work with the VRS on the 13th and 14th of July to lay ambushes, in the area described here including Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: No. No, no, we didn't get called out to do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you know -- I take it you know nothing about why the 2nd Company, your company, is noted taking part in those activities in this official bulletin?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Believe me, I don't know. I didn't find out anything about this. I didn't know anything about this bulletin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you were in Konjevic Polje on the 11th and early morning of the 12th, what Bratunac police officers were there then? There weren't too many, I take it. Do you remember which ones were there?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: First of all, there was Mirko Peric and I think Goran Ostojic was there, too, but I'm not sure about him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How about Dragisa Zekic?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Dragisa Zekic was a member of the 6th Company, and he was in Konjevic Polje at the time on combat duty. Most probably he was listed as performing combat duty at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see him there on the 11th or --

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: I don't remember, but I'm sure I did because he must have stopped by the checkpoint in Konjevic Polje, because they were billeted near the checkpoint in Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How about the 12th of July when you left -- when you say you left to Zvornik -- sorry, to Bratunac. Do you know if you saw Dragisa Zekic then?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this person by the name of Mirko, what was Mirko's last name?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Mirko Peric.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had he been a police officer in Bratunac before the war?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had something happened for him to lose his job?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes. Before the war, he lost his job. I don't know why, but during the war he was re-activated in the police station in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he ever a waiter when he was -- after loosing his job?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: At the Fontana Hotel. I don't know whether he worked in other catering facilities within the town area, but I know that he worked at the Hotel Fontana for sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you work with a Muslim before the war named Hasan Salihovic?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes. Hasan Salihovic. Should I give additional explanations?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: We finished school together. The school for internal affairs in Sarajevo, the police academy. We got our first jobs together. We were transferred to Srebrenica together. We were practically inseparable.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was his father's name?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: I think it was Hasib.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was the last time you saw him alive?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't see him during the war. Before the war, I was at their house. I even spent the night at their house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If we can go into private session just briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll go to private session, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The logbook abbreviation is BD. Borbena Dejstva. That means combat activities. Correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And we've heard your explanation of that. Do you stand by it today?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes. That abbreviation means combat activities, and that's that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you don't have any knowledge of what the 2nd Company was up to, whether they were laying ambushes in Ravni Buljim or assigned to Konjevic Polje or anything else outside of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: I don't know. But if I may explain?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: The first task of the 2nd Company, to the best of my knowledge, was, and that's where I was, to protect property in Srebrenica, to prevent any looting in Srebrenica, things like that. I did not have the opportunity of hearing any other orders or did I hear of anyone going to that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This logbook says you got to Srebrenica on the 21st, and before that you were involved in combat activities. Right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes. It says that I was transferred to the police station of public security in Srebrenica, on the 21st.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any re-direct?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Re-examined by Mr. Karnavas:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sticking with that logbook, on the 21st when you were transferred to the police station, in what capacity were you transferred as?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: I was transferred because I worked in Srebrenica before the war. And the order of the centre of public security head was that all the policemen who worked in Srebrenica before the war should return to the area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By that particular date, was the police station set up? Had it been re-activated completely and set up?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know exactly, but the organisation had already been established and some work was already being done.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, the Prosecutor asked you a question: How is it that this gentleman, Witness S, would single you out? Is it not a fact, sir, that yesterday you asked me to provide you the identity of the individual so you could sue that individual in courts for slandering you?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Leading and civil suits related to -- I don't see how it's relevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I don't think that is a leading question, because we mentioned that issue already. And you may proceed, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: But be careful that some of the testimony in the cross-examination was given in private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm not going to disclose anything, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall that, sir? Did you not ask me what procedures you could follow through in order to seek some sort of justice through the courts?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And upon asking me that question, I did not disclose to you who that individual was. Correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Correct, correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you were shown some bulletins. I just want to go through them just very quickly. The last -- and I'm referring to -- the first one is P4 -- 848. I don't know if it's -- if the gentleman has it. But if I could -- I just want to read the operation duty officer's name. Rodoljub Vidakovic. Do you know this gentleman?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: I do know Rodoljub Vidakovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, it says here that this was in Zvornik 12 July 1995. Did you see him on 12 July 1995? Did you have any contact with him, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: You mean Rodoljub Vidakovic?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: No, I had no contact with him, nor did I see him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And I take it the Prosecution didn't show you that either when they met with you back on 2001, the document so you could perhaps give them some explanation?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: No, they did not show it to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if I could show you the next exhibit, the next bulletin, which would be P849. We have the name of Vlado Kovacevic. And this is -- it says: "Zvornik, 14 July 1995." First of all, do you know Mr. Kovacevic?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: No. I don't know Vlado Kovacevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether someone from Zvornik contacted you that day for you to provide them with any information?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: No, no one contacted me and I was not in charge of that anyway.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the Prosecutor show you this document when they met with you back in 2001 so you could perhaps give them some sort of an explanation?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before coming here today, have you seen these documents before?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: No. I have never seen these documents before, the documents shown to me now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, going to the other exhibit, which was P847, that was the notebook. If we could hand the gentleman the original one. The Prosecution showed you one particular page, I think it was the 13th. I seem not to have it in my copy here of the exhibit. But that's where there seems to be some sort of a correction on the hours next to your name. Is that correct? The one that was pointed out to you by the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes. It can be seen here that some unnecessary things were done here in pencil, but I think that happened inadvertently.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, if you could look at that book, that logbook, at least tell us if that is the only correction that was made on that logbook, that we can perhaps then draw some conclusions. Do you see any other places where there might be corrections where somebody's name is erased or changed, dates have been -- or time periods have been re-marked over.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Well, on different pages, yes. On the first page, for instance, it says the 12th of July. Then there is the sector here and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you know why that was changed there?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Well, most probably because of some things that I believe were not intentional, because there are things like that on the other page, too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And if we were to go through this logbook, we would see a variation of corrections, would we not, where things have been crossed over, written over. Correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I take it you have no explanations as to why we have that?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: No, I do -- I have no explanations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before coming here today, have you seen this logbook before? Have you physically seen this logbook before?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Before, I saw it most probably at the police station in Srebrenica while I was on duty there, because this book was in the duty officer's room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. When was the last -- before coming here today and seeing this original one, when was the last time that you had seen this logbook?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: I last saw the logbook when we were over there, in Srebrenica. That was 1995. Later on I was not in a position to see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you transfer to Bratunac? Because you indicated to us that now you are a police officer at Bratunac. When did you transfer back?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: The police station in Bratunac you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. When did you transfer back to Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: In 1996, I was transferred to the border police, at my own request.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you know where this logbook has been kept all this time?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where the Prosecutor got a hold of this logbook before you saw it today?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: No, I did not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see this logbook before you went to have your interview with the Prosecutor's office back in 2001?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: In 1995, yes, but ever since, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. But I just want to make sure that we're clear. We know that you checked the other logbook that was in the safe in Bratunac before you went to your interview. My question is: Did you look at that logbook before going to meet with the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: No, I did not look at it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you give any instructions to anyone to go there, find it, and make corrections on July 13th?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: No, I did not. I gave no instructions in relation to this logbook.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Questions by the Judges. Judge Vassylenko. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Gospodin Deronjic, where were you during the nine days between 12 to 20 July 1995? In Srebrenica, or outside Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, throughout this time that you referred to, I was in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Was there combat activity in Srebrenica at that time?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: In that period of time, there was no combat activity in the town of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: But the logbook says that you participated in combat activity during these days.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: It was only the 2nd Company that was activated, and that was recorded here in the logbook as combat activities, while we went there to prevent looting, any harm done to property, and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: You mentioned the deputy commander of the Srebrenica police station, Petko Pavlovic. Do you know if he is still a police officer? And in that case, where he serves.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, Petko Pavlovic works in the state border service. He is the commander of the police station in Zvornik, of the border police, that is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: You also mentioned that deputy commander of the 2nd PJP was Goran Djelemic. Could you please spell his last name.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Goran, and then D-j-e-l-e-m-i-c.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Do you know where this man is today? Is he an active police officer, and if so, where he serves?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, Your Honour, I think that he is the commander of the police station of Kozluk, near Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: My last question: During the -- this critical period in July 1995, have you contacted Colonel Blagojevic or has Colonel Blagojevic contacted you?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I never had any personal contact with Mr. Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Hvala. I have no more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any questions out of Judge's questions? Mr. Karnavas?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Just one. Further examination by Mr. Karnavas:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I understand you correctly, is it the fact that you were activated into the 2nd Company that it's your understanding why it says "combat activity" here?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It's leading. It's the exact same leading question as before. The person has asked the question. It's too late. It's over.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm entitled to a clarification. That's why I phrased it, Your Honour. If it was my understanding so we have a clear record as to exactly what his understanding is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, try to rephrase your question, but you have to bear in mind that this question has been gone over many, many times.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just want to -- you've indicated to us that you were not involved in any combat activity once you went to Srebrenica. Could you please clarify for us: If you were not involved in any combat activity, why is it that it notes on the logbook -- why we have these initials "BD."

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Well, this is what it is about: In the logbook, in the duty roster book, the commander or the deputy commander wrote down combat activities because the 2nd Company was activated, because he could not record all of us. I mean, not the beat duty or other duties that took place in Srebrenica. I mean, he could not write down beat duty in Srebrenica or something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. One last question: You indicated on direct that your komandir was -- I believe it's Mladjenovic?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where he is located today and what he does?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mladjenovic is in Bratunac today. He is no longer a member of the police. I don't know what he does. He hasn't regulated his status anywhere yet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Very briefly. Further cross-examination by Mr. McCloskey:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This logbook where you were clarifying your response about that entry, did you look at this logbook and this entry before speaking to the Office of the Prosecutor in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't bring a copy of it and give it to the Prosecutor, though, did you?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're a police officer. You know how to get police reports and records and turn them over to prosecutors so people can be prosecuted, or not prosecuted?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: May I explain?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: When the investigator was questioning me, he told me where the book was and where I could check it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The OTP investigator? The Office of the Prosecutor investigator, sorry?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes. Should I say what his name is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's okay. Do you think he knew where this document was?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If I may be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.
