utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If I may be of some assistance, there might have been, I'm told, a mistranslation in the gentleman's previous answer. So if Mr. McCloskey could re-ask the question. That's what I'm told by my assistant who is fluent in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Which question? You have to identify it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The one preceding that, as far as who told whom where this logbook was located.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Maybe I can get --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The log -- you looked at this -- the logbook, the one that has got combat activities written on it prior to seeing Mr. -- I believe it was Mr. Ruez of the Office of the Prosecutor. Correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you told -- did you -- as you've said, you didn't bring a copy of that with you to the interview, did you?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Mr. Ruez -- do you recall Mr. Ruez saying something to you about this logbook?

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: Yes. He did say something to me. Can I tell you what it was?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: NENAD DERONJIC
utterances.text: He asked me where this book was, where I found it. And finally, he said that he would look for the book and that he didn't want this book to be destroyed if there was a flood or a fire or something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Nothing further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. At this stage are there any documents to tender? Mr. Karnavas?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we're tendering exhibit D124.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any objections, Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, if you are going to tender this document into evidence, we need some translations. Although you have used this document in the proceedings and some words have already been translated, at least we need a line indicating the -- what it means.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. So I will provide that, sir. It could be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, maybe only for this witness, number 26.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: As well as the front page of this document, if you have.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You mean the front page of the book itself?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, sure. So that we know where those contents come from.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So this document, D124, is admitted into evidence, pending the translation and front page, which will be submitted by the Defence counsel. And are there any documents for the Prosecution to tender?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Sorry. If there's more to this logbook, I assume Mr. Karnavas may have just had one page. But I think for the same reason that the front it would be a good idea to have copies of the entire book as well, if that's possible. And -- now, I've got a logbook as well as a couple of documents. And these documents and logbook are a little -- slightly different than the -- some of the other collections we have. And I think a proper foundation of them -- I can either provide a declaration of an investigator so you can see where they came from and when, or I can tell the Court as an officer of the court. But I think you should probably have a little more information before they come in. But I would be tentatively offering them now with a follow-up giving you information, which I think is appropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, can you indicate at this stage what are those documents that you are going to tender, just for the sake of the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Good point. The -- a copy of the logbook covering the dates of the police station, and the two bulletins, one that was dated 12 July and one that was dated 14 July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I guess that is document P847, 848, and 849.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, that's exactly right, as Ms. Stewart had in the outline.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Can I hear the initial response from Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, the initial response, Your Honour, is that we have no foundation, per se. We don't know where these documents came from. Obviously with respect to the bulletins, I suspect Mr. McCloskey wishes to tender them for the truth of the matter asserted in those particular documents, and I do have some problems with that. Having said all of that, the Prosecutor has indicated that he will be tendering these documents subject to connection, that down the road he will be connecting -- he will be laying the foundation or predicate for these documents to come in. Assuming that he will do that, I don't have a problem. So subject to connection, I don't have a problem to them coming in. But right now with what little we have, there -- I cannot object -- I cannot agree to have them come in without any further foundation. So -- but if I understood Mr. McCloskey correctly, he indicated that he would be providing us with some additional information. So in light of that, I think that they should not be admitted at this point in time until he connects them, unless, you know, we accept them subject to connection. If they don't connect, if they don't bring the foundation, then I would have the opportunity to make the request that the documents or these exhibits be disallowed from the collection of admitted evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, at this stage we'll not admit these three documents into the evidence, pending the submission by the Prosecution for any foundations. But generally speaking, we believe that these three documents are suitable for admission. But to be cautious we'll wait for a while until a later stage. It is so decided. Well, witness, thank you very much for coming to The Hague to give your evidence. When the court is adjourned, the usher will show you out of the room. We wish you a pleasant journey back home. The hearing is adjourned, and we'll resume tomorrow morning 9.00 in Courtroom II.
